sentences.text: The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the death of in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioners case is as under:
2.

That, on 22.9.2021 at about 7.30 a.m, the Parojan Das was proceeding in a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-04-JC-8172 as a pillion rider, said motor cycle was ridden by one Md.Isthiyak, when they reached near Sky walk of Manyatha Tech Park Gate, at that time, a container lorry bearing No.TN- 54-Q-7979 was proceeding ahead and followed by a autorickshaw bearing No.KA-03-AF-4604 and another autorickshaw bearing No.KA-04-AB-7892 and Maruthi Wagon R car bearing No.KA-50-M-6351, all of a sudden driver of the container lorry drove his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly took his vehicle towards his left, on account of sudden deviation, the driver of the autorickshaw and the car slow down their vehicles, at the same time, Bajaj Pulsar bearing No.KA-04-JC-8172 and another motor cycle bearing No.KA-50-EA-3166 slow down their bikes, in the same line the Tempo Traveller bearing No.KA-53-C-9548 without maintaining the safe distance dragged the hind portion of the bike.
On account of this, the bike dragged infront of the tempo traveller, it was made hit to front side car and autorickshaw.
In view of the serious nature of the accident the deceased was sitting as a pillion rider fell down from the bike, sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.

3. It is stated that, at the time of accident, deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 41 years, and doing tailes work and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m and contributing his entire earnings to maintain the family.
It is stated that, due to death of the deceased, the petitioners were put to great financial loss and mental agony.

It is further stated that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the drivers of Tempo Traveller bearing registration No.KA-53-C-9548 &
Container Lorry bearing registration No.TN-54-Q-7979.

It is stated that, respondent No.1 & 2 being insurer and the owner of the Tempo Traveller bearing No.KA-53-C- 9548 and the respondent No.3 & 4 are the insurer and owner of the Lorry bearing No.TN-54-Q-7979 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this petition.
4. After registration of the case, notices were issued to the respondents.

In response to the notices,
the respondent No.1 & 3 were appeared through their respective counsel and filed the written statements.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 & 4 did not appear before the court, remained absent, hence placed exparte.

5. In the written statement of the respondent No.2-insurance company contended that this respondent has issued two wheeler package policy bearing No.KA-53-C-9548 and not issued any policy in respect of the tempo traveller bearing No.KA-53-C- 9548.

Further contended that knowing the facts of the misrepresentation by the owner of the vehicle this respondent has canceled the policy on 30.6.2022 on the ground of misrepresentation of material facts.
Further contended that the driver of the tempo traveller had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle as on the date of accident.

Further contended that the owner of the tempo traveller had used his vehicle Bindu Devi vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128759098/
3 without valid permit and fitness certificate.

sentences.text: It is the defence of the respondent that accident was not occurred on account of rash and negligent driving of the Tempo Traveller bearing No.KA-53-C-9548, it is the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry bearing No.TN-54-Q-7979, autorickshaw bearing No.KA-03-AF-4604, KA-04-AB-7892 and car bearing No.KA-50-M-635, the rider of the motor cycle4 bearing No.KA-04-JC-8172 and KA-50-EA-3166.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.
6. The respondent No.3 in the written statement has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case.

Further contended that, the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of the driver of the tempo traveller, other motor vehicles drivers and riders, as they were proceeding near the place of accident without maintaining the safe distance between vehicles,
without having proper look drove the vehicles in a zig zag manner and caused the accident.

Further this respondent has admitted about the issuance of the police in respect of Lorry bearing registration No.TN-54-Q-7979 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It is also contention of the respondent No.3 that, the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence, permit and FC as on the date of the accident.

Further denied the age, income and avocation of the deceased and expenses incurred towards funeral and obsequies ceremony of the deceased and also denied the relationship of petitioners with the deceased.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

7. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this Tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that Parojan Das died due to the injuries sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 22.9.2021 at about 7.30 a.m. near Skywalk, Opp. Manyatha Tech Park, Outer Ring Road, Nagavara,
Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the drivers of the Tempo Traveller bearing No.KA-53-C- 9548 & Container Lorry bearing registration No.TN-54-Q-7979 in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation as prayed for?

If so, at what rate? from whom?
3) What order or award?
8.

In order to substantiate the case of the petitioners, petitioner No.3 examined himself as PW1 and got marked the documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P16.
9.
On the other hand, respondent No.1 examined its Manager-Legal Claims as RW1 and got marked one document as Ex.R1 to Ex.R3.
The respondent No.1 examined General Manager of M/s Paytm Insurance Broking Private Limited as RW2.

11. My findings to the above issues as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3:

R E A S O N S  ISSUE No.1:
12.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Tempo Traveller bearing registration No.KA-53-C-9548 and the driver of the Container Lorry bearing No.TN-54-Q-7979, the alleged accident had taken place, consequently Parojan Das died at the spot.
13.

On the other hand, the respondent No.1 being the insurer of the Tempo Traveller bearing No.KA-53-C-9548 has contended in its written statements that, accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the Container Lorry bearing No.TN-54-Q-7979, other motor vehicles, car and motor bikes and not on the part of the driver of the Tempo Traveller.

14. Further the respondent No.3 being the insurer of the Container Lorry bearing registration No.TN-54-Q-7979 have contended in its written statement that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the Tempo Traveller and other motor vehicles and riders of the motor bikes.
Hence, there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the Container Lorry.

15. On the basis of rival contention of both the parties, the petitioners have to place satisfactory evidence on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities against both the vehicles in question.
On the other hand, onus shifts on the respondents to prove the same by means of cogent and convincing evidence.
16. In order to prove their case, the petitioner No.3 examined himself as PW1.
In his examination- in-chief by way of affidavit, he has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of his oral evidence has relied upon Ex.
P1 to Ex

Ex.P1-true copy of the FIR, Ex.P2-true copy of the first information statement given by one Panthanaka Subramanyam, who is the driver of the Wagon Car bearing No.KA-50-M-6351, Ex.P3-true copy of spot sketch, Ex.P4-true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P5 to Ex.P7-true copies of IMV report, Ex.P8- Inquest report, Ex.P9-P.M. report and Ex.P10-true copy of charge sheet.

17. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by one Panthanaka Subramanyam, the S.H.O. of Chikkajala Traffic Police have registered the case against the drivers of both the vehicles for the offences punishable under section 279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC.

Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet alleging that the driver of the Tempo Traveller bearing No.KA-53-C-9548 and driver of the Container Lorry bearing Bindu Devi vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128759098/
5 No.TN-54-Q-7979 have committed the offences punishable under section 279, 337, 338 and 304(A)
of IPC.
18.
On the contrary, the respondent No.1 has examined its Manager-Legal as RW1.
He has reiterated the averments made in the written statement.
He has placed authorisation letter, policy copy and policy cancellation letter as per Ex.R1 to Ex.R3.
remained absent, placed exparte.
The respondent No.3 has not examined any witness on its behalf.
20. At the time of cross-examination of PW1, nothing has been elicited from his mouth to disbelieve the case of the petitioner.
Even at the time of cross-examination of RW1, it is clear that he has not challenged the charge sheet filed against the drivers of both the vehicle.
21. Added to this, on perusal of the recitals of the police documents, there is clear narration about the involvement of both the vehicles in the accident.
On keen observation of the evidence of PW1 and the documents produced by the petitioners, it is clear that due to the negligence of both the drivers of the offending vehicles the accident occurred.

22. Apart from this, there is no doubt that, the charge sheet submitted by the investigation officer clearly reveals that accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the Tempo Traveller bearing No.KA-53-C-9548 and the driver of the Container Lorry bearing registration No.TN-54-Q- 7979.
On perusal of the evidence and the materials placed by the petitioners, it is clear that the charge sheet is not the conclusive proof.
At the most, that may be a circumstance which has to be considered along with other materials on record.

23. On appreciation of evidence of PW1 and the documents placed by the petitioner, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the driver of the Tempo Traveller bearing No.KA-53-C-9548 and the driver of the Container Lorry bearing registration No.TN-54-Q-7979.
In the said accident, Parojan Das succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, I am answering the Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.2:
24.

Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.

Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.

At the same time, the documents produced by the petitioners, to prove their relationship with the deceased marked at Ex.P11 to Ex.P16 i.e., Aadhar card of the deceased,
death certificate and Aadhar cards of the petitioners have not been disputed by the other side.
The recitals of the above documents clearly speak about the relationship between the petitioners and the deceased.

sentences.text: Another aspect to be considered herein that, on going through the particulars of the petitioners mentioned in the cause title of the petition reflected that, the petitioner No.1 & 2 are children of the deceased have lost their love and affection of their father and the petitioner No.3 & 4 are the parents of the deceased have lost their son, who was the backbone of the family.
Hence, it is crystal clear that, the petitioners were dependents on the deceased during his lifetime.
26. The petitioners herein, have placed Aadhar card, which is marked at Ex.P11 to prove the actual age of the deceased as on the date of the accident.
On going through the said document, the date of birth of the deceased has been mentioned as 1.1.1980.
The accident occurred on 22.9.2021.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the deceased was aged about 41 years.
For his age, multiplier '14' is applicable as per the ratio in "Sarala Verma" Case.
27. In connection with the work of the deceased, in the main petition and also in the evidence of PW1 stated that, deceased was doing tiles work and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
The petitioners have not placed any documents to show the income of the deceased.
Hence, in the absence of the definite income of the deceased, it is opt to consider the notional income as per law.
It is pertinent to note that, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2021.
By keeping in mind about the year of the accident and also notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.15,000/- for the year 2021.
28. Apart from this, it is also relevant to discuss, that the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in, 2018 SAR (Civil) 81.

National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others,
"

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was observed that, "While determining the income, an addition of 50 per cent of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30 per cent, if the age of the deceased was between 40 and 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 and 60 years, the addition should be 15 per cent.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
In case the deceased was self- employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40 per cent of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 year.
An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years.

An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 and 50 years and 10 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 50-60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component. "

29. Having considered the above, as per law laid down in the above case, in connection with the deduction of personal and living expenses is concerned, it is settled that, "where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one third (1/8 th ) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, (1/4th) where the number of dependent family member is 4 to 6 and one fifth (1/5 th ) where the number of the dependent family members exceeds six."
30. In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, there are four persons were depending upon the income of the deceased.

Hence, as per the principle laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in Sarala Verma Case at para No.14, 1/4th has to be deducted towards personal and living Bindu Devi vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128759098/
7 expenses out of the total compensation.
31.

sentences.text: In the present case, deceased was aged about 41 years as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "14" is applicable.

And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through the nature of the occupation forthcoming in the petition averments, it is evident that, the deceased herein is not having permanent job and accurate income for consideration.
As such, deceased was comes under the purview of 40-50 years, 25% income of the deceased has to be taken into account towards future prospects.
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.15,000/- per month.
Annual income of the deceased was Rs.1,80,000/- per year.
Along with this, the future prospects of 25% is to be taken in to consideration, then the annual income of the deceased comes to (Rs.1,80,000+45,000) = Rs.2,25,000/-.
And 1/4th has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.

Thus, net loss of income comes to Rs.1,68,750/-
(Rs.2,25,000-Rs.56,250).

This income has to be multiplied by multiplier "14" which comes to Rs.23,62,500/-.
32.

Apart from this aspect, in connection with the loss of estate, consortium and with respect to the funeral expenses to calculate the quantum of the compensation under the aforesaid heads, it is relevant to note herein the following authority;
2018 SAR (Civil) 81.
National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others, The Hon'ble Apex Court discussed various aspects in connection with the claim petition filed by the claimants for compensation.

And also observed that while determining the claim petition, the reasonable figures on conventional heads, viz., loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/-
 and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The  aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

33. By relying upon the above said decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the amount of Rs.16,500/- is awarded under the head loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- is awarded towards funeral expenses and also by placing reliance upon the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited v/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Others, the amount of Rs.44,000/- each is awarded to the petitioner No.3 to 6 under the head loss of consortium.

LIABILITY:-
36.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Tempo Traveller bearing No.KA-53-C-9548 and driver of the Container Lorry bearing No.TN-54-Q-7979,
alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioners in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.
Therefore, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

37. It is the contention of the respondent No.1- insurer of the Tempo Traveller bearing No.KA-53-C- 9548 has contended in its written statement that, this respondent has issued two wheeler package policy bearing No.KA-53-C-9548 and not issued any policy in respect of the Tempo Traveller bearing No.KA-53-C-9548 as on the date of accident.

Further stated that after knowing the facts of the misrepresentation by the owner of the vehicle, this respondent has cancelled the policy on 30.6.2022 on the ground of misrepresentation of material facts.
Hence, this respondent is not liable to pay the compensation.
In order to substantiate its case, examined its Manager-Legal claims as RW1.
He has reiterated the averments made in the written statement.
He has placed authorisation letter, policy copy and policy cancellation letter.
During the course of cross-examination by the respondent No.3 stated that either owner of the vehicle or driver had not given information about the accident.
38. Further, examined General Manager at M/s Paytm insurance booking private limited as RW2.
He has deposed that their company is a direct insurance broker, an insurance intermediary duly registered with insurance regulatory and development authority of India.

The said company operates through on online digital platform (paytm app and website) which allows customers to Bindu Devi vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128759098/
9 compare and purchase insurance policies of various insurance companies.

sentences.text: The company solely facilitates the purchase of insurance products on its online platform based on customer input on the company's mobile application and website.
Further he has displayed the stage 1, in the stage-1 clearly mentioned the engine number D61003369 and chassis number MC1E4CEA8HP045618.
In the cross-examination he has admitted that his company is broker of TATA AIG insurance company.
They will collect the premium from customer and will be paid to the insurance company, the insurance company will issue policy.
Further, he has stated that, they have collected the vehicle information and the premium amount from the insured and sent the same to the insurance company.

39. It is pertinent to note that, on perusal of Ex.R2-policy copy, it clearly shows vehicle No.KA-53- C-9548, engine number D61003369 chassis number MC1E4CEA8HP045618, policy type two wheeler package policy, body type-- Scooter and seating capacity 2.

Over all appreciation of evidence of RW1 & RW2 and also by considering the documents placed by the RW1, it is clear that the owner of tempo traveller bearing No.KA-53-C-9548 has mispresented the class of vehicle to have undue benefit in lesser premium.
To eradicate the said fact, respondent No.2-owner of the Tempo Traveller has become silent spectator in this case.
Hence, the respondent No.2 being the owner is liable to pay the compensation.
The respondent No.1-insurance company has absolve from its liability.
40. Further as per the records insurance policy of the Lorry was valid from 16.7.2021 to 15.7.2022.
The alleged accident had taken place on 22.9.2021.
As such, I am of the view that, the respondent No.3 & 4 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy of the lorry bearing No.TN-54-Q-7979, the respondent No.3 is liable to pay the compensation at the ratio of 50% only and the remaining 50% shall be paid by the respondent No.2, being the owner of the Tempo Traveller bearing No.KA-53-C-9548.
The respondent No.2 and 3 are liable to pay interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
The petition against the respondent No.1-insurance company of the Tempo Traveller bearing No.KA-53-C-9548 is hereby dismissed.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
41.

In view of my due discussions on Issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act as against the respondent No.2, 3 & 4 is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act as against the respondent No.1 is hereby dismissed.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.25,71,500/- (Rupees twenty five lakh seventy one thousand and five hundred only) along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

The petitioner No.1 & 2 reported as dead during the pendency of the petition leaving behind other petitioner No.3 to 6 as their legal heirs.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.3 & 4 are entitled the share of 40% each, the petitioner No.5 & 6 are entitled the share of 10% each.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.3, 40% of the amount shall be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank of his choice for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released to him through due process of law.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.4, entire amount shall be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank of her choice till she attains age of majority or 3 years, whichever is later.
The guaridan of the petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time till she attains age of majority.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioenr No.5 & 6, by considering their age, entire amount shall be released to them through due process of law.

each.

On keen observation of the evidence of PW1 and the documents produced by the petitioners, it is clear that due to the negligence of both the drivers of the offending vehicles the accident occurred.
On perusal of the evidence and the materials placed by the petitioners, it is clear that the charge sheet is not the conclusive proof.
Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.
Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.
At the same time, the documents produced by the petitioners, to prove their relationship with the deceased marked at Ex.P11 to Ex.P16 i.e., Aadhar card of the deceased,
death certificate and Aadhar cards of the petitioners have not been disputed by the other side.

Hence, it is crystal clear that, the petitioners were dependents on the deceased during his lifetime.
The petitioners have not placed any documents to show the income of the deceased.
Hence, in the absence of the definite income of the deceased, it is opt to consider the notional income as per law.

29. Having considered the above, as per law laid down in the above case, in connection with the deduction of personal and living expenses is concerned, it is settled that, "where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one third (1/8 th ) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, (1/4th) where the number of dependent family member is 4 to 6 and one fifth (1/5 th ) where the number of the dependent family members exceeds six."
Hence, as per the principle laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in Sarala Verma Case at para No.14, 1/4th has to be deducted towards personal and living Bindu Devi vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128759098/
7 expenses out of the total compensation.
31.
In the present case, deceased was aged about 41 years as on the date of the accident.
And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through the nature of the occupation forthcoming in the petition averments, it is evident that, the deceased herein is not having permanent job and accurate income for consideration.
As such, deceased was comes under the purview of 40-50 years, 25% income of the deceased has to be taken into account towards future prospects.
National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others, The Hon'ble Apex Court discussed various aspects in connection with the claim petition filed by the claimants for compensation.
Therefore, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, the respondent No.2 being the owner is liable to pay the compensation.
The respondent No.1-insurance company has absolve from its liability.
The alleged accident had taken place on 22.9.2021.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.15,000/- per month.
Along with this, the future prospects of 25% is to be taken in to consideration, then the annual income of the deceased comes to (Rs.1,80,000+45,000) = Rs.2,25,000/-.
And 1/4th has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.
The  aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
Accordingly, the petitioners herein are entitled to get total compensation of Rs.25,71,500/-
(Rupees twenty five lakh seventy one thousand and five hundred only), along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka in MFA No.103557/2016, between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.
As such, I am of the view that, the respondent No.3 & 4 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
In view of the valid insurance policy of the lorry bearing No.TN-54-Q-7979, the respondent No.3 is liable to pay the compensation at the ratio of 50% only and the remaining 50% shall be paid by the respondent No.2, being the owner of the Tempo Traveller bearing No.KA-53-C-9548.
The respondent No.2 and 3 are liable to pay interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
The petition against the respondent No.1-insurance company of the Tempo Traveller bearing No.KA-53-C-9548 is hereby dismissed.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
